entry.title: Mend for GitHub Enterprise: Version 26.9.1.4 (01-October-2026)
entry.content:
Resolved Issues

  • Fixed an issue where long-running issue publishing processes failed due to GitHub installation access token expiration. The system now proactively refreshes tokens before they expire, ensuring uninterrupted synchronization for large repositories.

  • Introduced a new configuration parameter, `issue.update.pause`, to independently control the delay after issue updates and closures, to solve an issue of tied throttling pauses. This allows for more granular performance tuning by separating update pauses from creation pauses, optimizing SCM API interactions and reducing the risk of rate limiting without affecting existing creation workflows.

  • Fixed an issue where the controller incorrectly ignored errors returned with an HTTP 200 status. The controller now correctly identifies and logs these error responses, improving diagnostic capabilities for startup failures.

  • Fixed an issue where attempting to rebuild the integration's scanner image would fail due to a missing Scala package. The issue only affected setups with Scala enabled.

entry.title: Mend for GitHub.com: Version 26.9.1 (27-September-2026)
entry.content:
New Features and Updates

  • (SCA) (Open Beta) Mend for GitHub.com now supports the Bun package manager for JavaScript projects. This update allows for the automatic detection and reporting of both direct and transitive dependencies in projects using `package.json` alongside `bun.lock` or `bun.lockb` files, ensuring secure and reliable dependency management for the Bun ecosystem.

  • (SCA) Python constraints.txt files are now supported. This update allows the scanner to identify and apply dependency constraints, including those for transitive dependencies, without requiring manual references in requirements.txt. By honoring these constraints during resolution, the system reduces false-positive vulnerability reports and ensures scan results accurately reflect the specific package versions permitted in your environment.

  • (SAST) Increased the maximum comment length for the `/mend code suppress` and `/mend code comment` commands in GitHub to 65,536 characters. This update ensures that full technical justifications and detailed audit records are preserved without truncation, matching the character limits of the Mend Platform and GitHub.

  • (SAST) The integration now supports selecting which languages to scan, using the new algoLangs field in .mendsastcli-config.json. Until now, narrowing what a scan covered meant listing numeric engine IDs in the engines field. You can now specify languages by name instead, which is quicker to write and far easier to understand when someone reviews the configuration later.

Resolved Issues

  • (SCA) Fixed an issue where GitHub check-run updates were rejected with a "summary exceeds a maximum bytesize of 65535" error. The truncation logic was updated to ensure accuracy for multi-byte characters. Additionally, a maximum count was implemented for the resolved vulnerabilities section to prevent it from exceeding size constraints. These changes ensure that scan results are correctly surfaced on pull requests even with large result sets.

  • (SAST) Fixed an issue where manual SAST scans on non-default branches incorrectly tagged the project with the repository's default branch name. This fix ensures that the project tag accurately reflects the specific branch being scanned, maintaining consistency between the project metadata and the scanned commit.

  • (SAST) Fixed an issue where SAST results publishing jobs would fail with a 401 error if the session JWT expired during long-running processes. The system now automatically refreshes the session token and retries the request, ensuring that publishing jobs complete successfully regardless of duration.

entry.title: Mend Unified Agent: Version 26.9.1 (28-September-2026)
entry.content:
Resolved Issues

  • Fixed an issue where Python scans incorrectly reported zero dependencies when `python.localPackagePathsToInstall` was configured alongside a hierarchy tree. This occurred due to a parsing error in the dependency tree resolution that caused the entire manifest to be discarded if specific local packages or tooling artifacts could not be matched. The resolution logic has been corrected to ensure all identified dependencies are accurately reported.

  • Fixed an issue where using the -f or -file flag in `maven.additionalArguments` caused standard `pom.xml` files to be ignored and prevented the detection of nested manifests. The Maven resolver now correctly identifies both custom-named manifests and standard project files, supports all valid Maven flag formats, and ensures that quiet mode flags do not interfere with dependency resolution results.

  • Fixed an issue where transient network faults originating from packages other than `java.net`, such as `org.apache.http`, were incorrectly classified as permanent failures. This caused the Unified Agent to ignore the configured connection retry policy and abort the scan on the first attempt. The classification logic has been updated to ensure all recoverable I/O faults are properly retried, improving scan stability during intermittent network instability.

  • Fixed an issue where NuGet scans incorrectly reported phantom library versions in the inventory. This occurred when a package's declared dependency version differed from the version actually restored, and the restored version was missing from the global NuGet cache. The resolver now correctly validates dependency versions against the local restore directory, ensuring accurate inventory reporting.

entry.title: Mend CLI: Version 26.9.1 (28-September-2026)
entry.content:
New Features and Updates

  • (SCA) (Open Beta) The Mend CLI now supports the Bun package manager for JavaScript projects. This update allows for the automatic detection and reporting of both direct and transitive dependencies in projects using `package.json` alongside `bun.lock` or `bun.lockb` files, ensuring secure and reliable dependency management for the Bun ecosystem.

  • (SAST) The Mend CLI SAST scan (mend code) now supports a --print-to-console flag that prints the CLI logs directly to the console (stdout) as the scan runs, in addition to writing them to the log file. Previously this was only available for SCA scans (mend dep).

  • (SAST) Default exclusions in mend code CLI scans now ignore /_MACOSX/..* metadata files across all SAST scan engines. This update prevents macOS-specific system files from interfering with the TreeSitter parser during scans on Windows environments, ensuring more stable and accurate analysis. These exclusions are applied automatically via centralized settings, even when default exclusions are otherwise disabled.

Resolved Issues

  • Updated the third-party Go components bundled inside the CLI binaries.

  • (SCA) Fixed an issue where the CLI incorrectly reported a successful scan with exit code 0 when required lockfiles, such as composer.lock or package-lock.json, were missing. The detection logic now ensures that a warning is correctly logged and preserved when a manifest file is identified without its corresponding lockfile, providing better visibility into scan integrity.

  • (Container) Fixed an issue where the CLI local JSON export displayed a severity label that contradicted the CVSS score band within the same finding record. The export now ensures that the severity label and CVSS score are derived from the same source, providing consistent and accurate vulnerability data.

  • (Container) Fixed an issue where `mend image --tar` failed to scan container image tarballs exported in pure OCI format. The scanner previously required a Docker-specific `manifest.json` file, which is not present in spec-compliant OCI image layouts. The CLI now correctly handles OCI-layout archives, including `index.json` and OCI-compliant blob structures, ensuring successful SBOM generation and vulnerability scanning for OCI-format exports.

  • (SAST) Fixed an issue where SAST scans failed to return exit code 9 and did not break the pipeline, even when workflow violations were detected and the "Fail Pipeline on Violation" setting was enabled. The CLI now correctly enforces workflow policies by returning the appropriate exit code to ensure pipeline failures occur as expected when security violations are identified.

  • (SAST) Fixed an issue in the Mend CLI where users with non-English characters in their profile names were denied access due to incorrect JWT decoding. The authentication process now correctly handles special characters to ensure seamless access for all users.

entry.title: Mend AI: Version 25.12.1 (05-January-2026)
entry.content:
New Features and Updates

  • (Premium / Core) Introducing System Prompt Risk (open beta), a new detection and remediation offering by Mend AI, for mitigating risks posed by system prompts used in conversational AI interfaces.

    • A new System Prompt Risk table inventories system prompts and provides quick export/sharing and deep-link side panel for prompt context.

    • System Prompt Risks are integrated into the existing AI Security Risk Factors across Projects and Applications. The classification appears as a Conversational Interface chip, is filterable, and automatically participates in dashboards and workflows.

    • Remediation in the form of a hardened system prompt is available in the System Prompt side panel, providing clear, copy-ready remediation guidance for AppSec engineers and developers.

    • The AI Security Dashboard has been enriched with system prompt risk data.

    • System prompt risk data is also available via API.

entry.title: Mend Container: Version 26.9.2 (04-October-2026)
entry.content:
New Features and Updates

  • The image scan size limit for Mend Container has been increased from 2GB to 4GB. This update allows for the successful pulling, extraction, and scanning of larger container images across all registry integrations, including ECR. Scans for images exceeding the new 4GB limit will now provide a clear error message. Additionally, scanner stability and timeouts have been optimized to accommodate the increased data volume, ensuring accurate reporting of vulnerabilities, licenses, and components in the platform UI.

Resolved Issues

  • Fixed an issue where the severity distribution in the `mend image` JSON report did not match the Platform UI for the same scan. This discrepancy, which caused some findings to be reported at a higher severity level in the JSON output, has been resolved to ensure consistency across all reporting interfaces.

entry.title: Mend SAST: Version 26.9.2 (05-October-2026)
entry.content:
New Features and Updates

  • Mend SAST now supports additional configuration files, such as YAML and JSON, to improve entry point detection. The engine automatically identifies API endpoints and maps them to their corresponding implementation classes. This enhancement ensures comprehensive security coverage for contract-first applications by automatically marking all generated entry point parameters as tainted, eliminating the need for manual configuration of custom frameworks.

  • Improved the accuracy of the Python engine across the following CWEs:

    • CWE-022 Path Traversal

    • CWE-078 OS Command Injection

    • CWE-079 XSS

    • CWE-089 SQL Injection

    • CWE-094 Code Injection

    • CWE-209 Error Message Info Exposure

    • CWE-295 Improper Cert Validation

    • CWE-532 Sensitive Info in Log

    • CWE-601 Open Redirect

    • CWE-918 SSRF

    • CWE-943 NoSQL Injection

Resolved Issues

  • Fixed an issue where the entry resolver failed when scanning certain AWS Lambda handler files in TypeScript.

entry.title: Mend SCA: Version 26.9.2 (04-October-2026)
entry.content:
New Features and Updates

  • Email notification capabilities in Automation Workflows have been enhanced, allowing workflow creators to directly control recipients by selecting specific users or groups for scan summary emails. Additionally, a new "Send Email" action has been introduced to notify you of new findings—such as newly published CVEs—independent of scans, with configurable delivery frequencies.

    • Dedicated zero-day alerts have been added, to ensure immediate awareness when your organization is vulnerable to emerging threats.

Resolved Issues

  • Fixed an issue where Package Health data was missing in the Remediation tab for scoped npm packages. The platform now correctly URL-encodes scoped package names when querying the health API, ensuring accurate display of age, adoption, compatibility, and confidence metrics.

entry.title: Mend AppSec Platform: Version 26.9.2 (04-October-2026)
entry.content:
New Features and Updates

  • (SCA) Email notification capabilities in Automation Workflows have been enhanced, allowing workflow creators to directly control recipients by selecting specific users or groups for scan summary emails. Additionally, a new "Send Email" action has been introduced to notify you of new findings—such as newly published CVEs—independent of scans, with configurable delivery frequencies.

    • Dedicated zero-day alerts have been added, to ensure immediate awareness when your organization is vulnerable to emerging threats. These alerts can be switched off for individual organizations you're a member of or all of them (My Profile → Email Notifications).

Resolved Issues

  • (SCA) Fixed an issue where Package Health data was missing in the Remediation tab for scoped npm packages. The platform now correctly URL-encodes scoped package names when querying the health API, ensuring accurate display of age, adoption, compatibility, and confidence metrics.

  • (IaC) Fixed an issue where the IaC scanner incorrectly flagged Dockerfiles as using unpinned base images when the image version was defined via a build argument default. Additionally, the remediation guidance for this policy was corrected to ensure it no longer suggests using the "latest" tag.
